instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Prick the 3 eggplants all over with a fork and set them on a foil lined baking sheet.

Roast the eggplants for about 40 minutes, turning them over halfway, until the skins are wrinkled and charred and the eggplants have collapsed. If you have a gas burner, you can char them right over the flame instead, turning them every few minutes, for a smokier taste.
Meanwhile, cut the 1 1/4 lb lamb into 1 inch cubes. Pat them dry and toss them with 1 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the black pepper.
Finely chop the onion and the green pepper. Mince the 2 garlic cloves. Grate 4 oz of the cheese, about 1 cup.

Heat 1 tbsp of the butter and 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium high. Add the lamb in a single layer and leave it for 2 to 3 minutes, until the underside is browned. Turn the pieces and brown the other sides for 2 minutes more, then move the lamb to a plate.
Add the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil, the onion and the green pepper to the pot. Cook for about 5 minutes, stirring, until they're soft and starting to color.
Add the garlic, 1 tbsp tomato paste and 1 tbsp red pepper paste and stir for 1 minute, until the pastes turn a shade darker.

Put the lamb and its juices back in, add the can of diced tomatoes and 1/3 cup water, and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer for 50 to 60 minutes, until the lamb is tender and the sauce is thick.
When the eggplants are done, let them cool for 10 minutes. Split them open, scoop the flesh into a colander and throw away the skins and stems. Let the flesh drain for 10 minutes.
Chop the eggplant flesh finely, put it in a bowl and mash it with the juice of half the lemon.
Warm the 2 1/2 cups milk in a small saucepan or the microwave until it's steaming.
Melt the remaining 4 tbsp butter in a medium saucepan over medium. Stir in the 1/2 cup flour and cook it for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until it smells nutty but hasn't browned.
Pour in the warm milk a splash at a time, whisking after each one so no lumps form. Keep whisking for about 4 minutes, until the sauce is thick enough to coat a spoon.
Stir in the eggplant, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the remaining 1/4 tsp black pepper and cook for 2 minutes. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the grated cheese until it melts.
Chop a small handful of the parsley.
Taste the stew. If it's flat, add salt first, then a squeeze of lemon from the other half.
Spread the eggplant sauce over each plate, spoon the lamb stew into the middle and scatter the parsley over the top.
method_notes: All three read versions put browned lamb over a smoky eggplant puree. Ozlem's Turkish Table and Turkeys for Life simmer the lamb with onion, garlic and tomato for about an hour and fold roasted eggplant into a butter, flour and milk sauce with grated cheese; Ozlem adds green pepper and Turkish red pepper paste, and suggests baking the eggplants at 425°F when there's no open flame. SBS (Adam Liaw's version) is a quick one: seared lamb fillet with olives, cumin and isot pepper over an eggplant puree made with cream and kaşar instead of a roux. This one follows Ozlem's. No version had 20 or more ratings and RecipeTin Eats (the trusted cook for Turkish) has no version, so the first read version leads.
